Battery electrode microscopy QC: batch comparison with no reference batch

31 SEM sites in 3 batches. Per-site spatial Gaussian Processes give each microstructure KPI with an honest error bar, then every batch is compared with all the other sites.

Verdict per batch

No batch is used as a reference. Each batch is compared with all other sites pooled. Without a material specification, “outlier” means different, not defective.

Batch_1 Investigate Strongest differences vs the other sites: Si area fraction higher by 0.021 (effect size +1.2, adjusted p=0.118); Si particle solidity (0-1) lower by 0.014 (effect size -1.1, adjusted p=0.117). Unusual individual sites: 4ih2ggld (Si area fraction, Si particle solidity (0-1)); 5n1q8atc (Si area fraction, Si particle solidity (0-1)). The batch average is not decisively different; the verdict comes from multiple unusual sites.

Batch_2 Consistent Strongest differences vs the other sites: Si particles per 1000 µm² lower by 0.569 (effect size -0.4, adjusted p=1.000); Pore patch size, GP lengthscale (µm) lower by 0.096 (effect size -0.4, adjusted p=1.000). None of these is larger than normal site-to-site variation.

Batch_3 Consistent Strongest differences vs the other sites: Si particle d90 (µm) lower by 0.424 (effect size -0.7, adjusted p=0.446); Si area fraction lower by 0.011 (effect size -0.6, adjusted p=1.000). Unusual individual sites: hzumfsms (Pore patch size, GP lengthscale (µm)).

How the verdict is decided
  • Outlier: a KPI differs with Holm-adjusted permutation p<0.01 and effect size |d|≥0.8.
  • Investigate: adjusted p<0.05, or the batch is significantly more variable (spread p<0.01), or at least 2 sites are individually unusual (robust z>3.5 vs all other sites).
  • Consistent: none of the above. This means “no evidence of change”, which is weaker with few sites.

Imaging confounds and limits

These KPIs also track imaging conditions, so part of their variation may come from the microscope rather than the material:

  • Porosity (area fraction) vs BSE black-level offset (>10): median 0.051 with vs 0.064 without (p=0.027)
  • Porosity (area fraction) vs BSE Si/graphite contrast (si_peak): Spearman ρ=-0.50 (p=0.004)
  • Phase-boundary density (µm/µm²) vs BSE Si/graphite contrast (si_peak): Spearman ρ=-0.66 (p=<0.001)
  • Pore patch size, GP lengthscale (µm) vs BSE black-level offset (>10): median 1.81 with vs 2.01 without (p=0.027)
  • Pore patch size, GP lengthscale (µm) vs BSE Si/graphite contrast (si_peak): Spearman ρ=-0.37 (p=0.042)
  • Only 7, 7 and 17 sites per batch: “consistent” is weak evidence of no change, especially for Batch_1 and Batch_2.
  • Phase identity (bright = Si) is inferred from BSE brightness and the dataset description, not confirmed.
  • Without an approved reference or specification, the system can say which batch differs and how, not whether it is acceptable.

Method

  1. Load each site from the PMDB half-resolution cache (50 nm/px, raw uint8 BSE).
  2. Normalise BSE per image: 0 = its own pore-black level, 1 = its own graphite peak. No batch-wide threshold, so the Batch_3 black-level offset is absorbed.
  3. Segment: pore below 0.5; bright phase above the histogram valley before the bright peak; graphite/binder in between.
  4. Cut into 64 px (3.2 µm) tiles; compute porosity, Si fraction, graphite fraction and phase-boundary density per tile.
  5. Fit one GP per KPI per site on tile position (RBF + white noise). Keep the GP mean, its correlated-error standard error (1/√(1ᵀK⁻¹1)) and the lengthscale in µm.
  6. Particle KPIs (d50, d90, count, solidity) from connected bright regions.
  7. Compare batches with site as the unit: permutation tests, bootstrap CIs, Holm correction over KPIs, spread test, robust-z site flags, and confound checks.

Surprise batch: copy it to PMDB/data/Batch_N and run ./run_all.sh. Nothing is retrained; the new batch is compared with all other sites.

Data: PMDB repository (jkz22/PMDB), half-resolution cache, 50 nm/px. KPIs come from BSE segmentation with per-image intensity anchoring. Statistics: site is the unit, with permutation tests, bootstrap 95% CIs and Holm correction across 9 KPIs. Phase identity (bright = Si) is inferred, not confirmed. No batch is treated as approved, so verdicts mean different or not different, not good or bad.
